messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: KV cache eviction rate + write amplification spike on cluster eu-west-1. Continuous-batching queue depth rising, streaming token latency increasing. Auto-severity: 2. Links: https://dash.redwood/eu-west1/cache /logs?query=eviction_spike

alice (oncall): I’m paged, looking now. TL;DR: large cache growth started ~1768504200, corresponds with a config rollout last night (batching window relax). Impact: streaming responses stalled (~10-30s token gaps) for ~5% of requests in the last 15m.

alice (oncall): Adding eng-runtime and SRE. @ben @carla please ack.

ben (eng-runtime): ack. I’m checking the batch router and kv-metrics. Seeing sustained continuous-batch sizes 3x normal and KV hotset size doubling. suspect batching cadence regression interacting with prefetch/eviction.

carla (sre): ack. I’ll start triage runbook. Any customer-facing errors? @megan

megan (customer-success): Two customers reported intermittent streaming disconnects and slow tails. Neither entirely down but high error rate on streaming chunked responses. I’m preparing a TTR note.

ops_jeff: grabbing logs, linking tail: https://logs.redwood/1768504321/streaming

devops-bot: Grafana snapshot attached: https://grafana.redwood/snapshot/abc123 (eviction rate, batch_depth, token_latency)

ben (eng-runtime): Quick idea: roll batch window back to previous safe value and drain continuous-batching queue for 30m; that should reduce amplification. I can push a config override to canary in 2m.

carla (sre): +1. Also suggest enabling aggressive kv.eviction.temp_ttl=60s for the affected pool to limit hotset growth while we assess.

sam (eng-ml): heads-up: partial flush bug might be triggered by this cadence — we’re seeing some streaming sessions that never flush partial outputs until the KV boundary is hit. That explains token cadence stalls.

alice (oncall): Priority mitigation plan: 1) config rollback (batch window -> previous) to canary 2) set kv.temp_ttl 60s on affected shards 3) watch streaming token latency 4) engage a quick hotfix for partial-flush if it recurs.

ben (eng-runtime): Applying canary override now: `curl -XPOST https://config.redwood/api/v1/overrides -d '{"target":"eu-west-1","key":"batch.window_ms","value":75}'`

ben (eng-runtime): Also nuking continuous batch backlog on canary nodes. running: ```for pod in $(kubectl get pods -l app=batch-runner -n eu-west -o name); do kubectl exec $pod -- /bin/sh -c 'service batch-runner flush-queue'; done```

carla (sre): Patch kv eviction: `POST /internal/kv/evict?pool=eu-west&ttl=60` (internal-only) applied.

devops-bot: Canary metrics: batch_depth -> down 65% in 3m, eviction_rate -> normalized, streaming token tail latency p50 -> unchanged, p95 -> improving.

megan (customer-success): Customer A reporting improvement on canary path; Customer B still seeing occasional 15s stalls. Not all traffic routed to canary yet.

sam (eng-ml): Reproduced partial flush locally with the sequence that matches the current config: batching window extension + mid-stream prefetch eviction triggers. Quick code change: ensure `flush_partial_output()` called after KV page boundary. I'll prepare a trivial patch (1-line) and a canary build.

ben (eng-runtime): If we can get a patch in <20m, we can deploy to canary and then prod. Otherwise we should continue config mitigation and route critical customers to dedicated pool.

alice (oncall): Decision: do both. Ben/Carla proceed with config rollback + eviction TTL. Sam, fast patch to canary. @dmitri can you prepare routing rule to divert 10% of traffic from top 5 affected customers to dedicated pool?

dmitri (infra): I can do 10% diversion via the smart-router in 8m. will coordinate with megan for customer targeting.

ben (eng-runtime): Patch built and deployed to canary: `service-runtime v3.4.1-hotfix` includes `flush_partial_output()` change. Monitoring canary now.

devops-bot: Canary streaming token stalls reduced to near zero in the instances with hotfix. Metrics snapshot: https://grafana.redwood/snapshot/def456

carla (sre): Rolling patch to 30% of prod nodes now. Watching for regressions.

alice (oncall): Any errors introduced? watch for increased CPU due to extra flush calls.

ben (eng-runtime): CPU delta negligible on canary. No increased error rates. Proceeding to full rollout at steady rate.

megan (customer-success): Notifying impacted customers: short note saying we’ve applied mitigations, some traffic rerouted, expect full recovery within 45m. Will send targeted follow-ups if any remaining issues.

devops-bot: Prod rollout 0->100% in progress: 0% -> 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% (rolling). ETA to 100% ~ 27m.

alice (oncall): Observed behaviour: eviction rate peaked at 14k/s, now back to baseline ~900/s. Streaming p95 token latency from 18s -> 0.9s over the rollout. Error rate for streaming endpoints down to normal.

ops_jeff: Confirmed logs show flush calls correlated with fix. Example trace: ```TRACE session=abcd token_gap=0.02s flush_called=true```

megan (customer-success): Customer B confirmed recovery on diverted traffic; full path recovery in 12m on their end.

carla (sre): Marking incident as mitigated. Creating incident timeline. Need follow-ups: root cause RCA, revert-proofing config rollout, more robust preflight checks for continuous-batching rollouts, and a load-test for partial-flush scenarios.

sam (eng-ml): Action: add unit + integration test covering batch-window+eviction interplay and partial flush. I’ll own the tests.

ben (eng-runtime): Action: add guard in router that refuses batch.window_ms increases >2x in a single rollout without canary confirmation. I’ll file PR.

dmitri (infra): Action: add temporary dashboard alert for batch_depth * eviction_rate > threshold to catch similar amplification earlier.

alice (oncall): Handing off to next oncall (carla) for post-deploy verification and PM/RCA follow-up. Next check-in in 6h. If anything regresses ping this thread.

carla (sre): acked, taking handoff. Please add any leftover logs and lane details to the incident doc.

megan (customer-success): Customer comms sent, customers looped into a post-incident call tomorrow.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated -> creating incident record ID INC-2026-042. Add notes: mitigation: config rollback + kv-temp-ttl + partial-flush hotfix v3.4.1-hotfix.

alice (oncall): Filing follow-up tickets: INC-2026-042-RCA, P1:guard-batch-rollouts, P2:add-load-test-partial-flush. Assigned as discussed.

ben (eng-runtime): quick snippet of the hotfix log for the record: ```2026-03-15T10:12:45Z runtime: flush_partial_output triggered session=abcd shard=eu-west reclaimed=12ms```

carla (sre): Closing on-call handoff. All good for now. :thumbsup:

alice (oncall): Great job team. Postmortem owners: ben (root-cause + rollout process), sam (tests + flush coverage), dmitri (alerts), megan (customer comms).
